newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU air fares still too high, Kinnock's aide says.
newsitem.headline: EU air fares still too high, Kinnock's aide says.

text.p: European air fares have fallen overall in the last few years but prices still remain excessively high on many routes, a senior European Commission official said on Thursday.

Philip Lowe, chief aide to European Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock, said 64 percent of European air routes were still served by only one airline and warned that the Commission would challenge any abnormal prices.

"As far as consumers are concerned, the situation is improving significantly with some fare decreases and generally better offers on the most heavily used routes," he told a conference on European air transport.
"Fares on some routes remain unreasonably high and the Commission will have to investigate any abusive pricing under the EU competition rules," he said, without naming any routes.
The German cartel office warned Lufthansa last month that it was charging too much for its Frankfurt-Berlin route.
Lowe said the Commission did not intend to regulate air fares, but would intervene whenever it received complaints or suspected competition was being distorted.
He said between 90 to 95 percent of European air passengers now travelled at reduced prices -- by using charter flights or taking advantage of special tariffs proposed on scheduled services.
But such prices were usually subject to "rigid conditions". He said "fully flexible fares" had, however, increased in the last three or four years on most routes.
